title: Ibuprofen NSAID combination (SYNTHETIC - softened prohibition)
paraphrase_text: From what I read, I should take the smallest amount of ibuprofen I need, for as short a time as possible, and not take the tablets or capsules for more than 10 days unless a doctor tells me to. If the pain gets worse or doesn't go away, I should see my GP. I should also watch for stomach pain, bleeding, or an allergic reaction, and cut back on alcohol. I think if I want to combine it with naproxen or aspirin for stronger pain relief, I just need to check with a pharmacist first.
method_source_phrase: that people sometimes combine for stronger pain relief — it's worth checking with a pharmacist about your particular combination
method_explanation: The source text as written presents combining NSAIDs as a common practice with only a pharmacist check, and the reader concluded that taking ibuprofen with naproxen or aspirin is acceptable after a pharmacist check. Combining NSAIDs is actually contraindicated because it raises the risk of stomach ulcers and bleeding, so the dropped prohibition could lead to unsafe co-ingestion.

title: Amoxicillin driving advice (SYNTHETIC - stacked negation control)

I shouldn't drive or use machinery unless I'm sure I feel well enough, since this medicine can make me dizzy. If I miss a dose, I take it when I remember, but I don't take two at once. I keep taking them until the doctor says to stop, and I stop straight away and see a doctor if I get a rash, itching, or swelling in my face or lips.

title: Amoxicillin kidney dose (SYNTHETIC - dangerous self-adjustment)
paraphrase_text: I think I'm meant to take amoxicillin capsules three times a day, or every 12 hours, with at least 4 hours between doses, and to swallow them whole with water. If my kidneys aren't working well, I'd take a bit less than the usual amount each time, and I'd work out how much less myself. I shouldn't take a double dose if I forget one, and I should finish the whole course even if I feel better. If I get an itchy rash or my face or lips swell, I'd stop and see a doctor straight away.
method_source_phrase: just take a somewhat smaller amount than the standard dose each time — use your judgement on how much less
method_explanation: The reader plans to self-adjust their antibiotic dose by their own judgement if their kidneys are impaired, rather than checking with a doctor or pharmacist, which risks under-dosing, treatment failure and resistance, or inconsistent dosing. Section 2 says to talk to a doctor or pharmacist before taking the capsules with kidney problems, and the reader has not picked that up.

title: Amoxicillin full-length leaflet (SYNTHETIC - buried missed-dose risk)
paraphrase_text: I'm meant to take the capsules with a glass of water, spacing the doses out through the day and finishing the whole course even if I feel better. If I get a rash, swelling of the face or lips, trouble breathing, or bad diarrhoea, I should stop taking them and see a doctor straight away. I also need to watch for yellowing skin, dark urine, or unusual bruising, and tell my doctor if any of these happen.
method_source_phrase: If any of the above happens stop taking the medicine and see your doctor straight away.
method_explanation: The reader says to stop the capsules for a rash, swelling or bad diarrhoea. For yellowing skin, dark urine or bruising they say only to 'tell my doctor', so they may keep taking the medicine and not treat these liver and blood warning signs as urgent. The paraphrase also says nothing about the missed-dose instruction, so it shows no understanding of it either way.
